propositions: A committed lock freezes transitive dependencies, causing published advisories on pinned versions to block all unrelated changes simultaneously
The Gerrit verify gate now blocks only when a change touches the dependency map (uv.lock, pyproject.toml, requirements files); unrelated changes are unblocked
The scheduled main/release lane blocks advisory findings and escalates via a daily canary that deduplicates and files tickets following the bridge-canary pattern
Severity filtering applies: CRITICAL/HIGH fail the gate, MEDIUM warns, LOW is tracked; unrated advisories are treated as HIGH by default

override-dependencies is the correct remedy for upstream-capped vulnerable versions, requiring documented justification and a REMOVE-WHEN condition; constraint-dependencies and uv lock --upgrade-package are ineffective against caps

The runbook documents the uv resolution mechanics (universal resolution locks all extras jointly), distinguishes real findings from flakes (recheck works only for DB-UNREACHABLE), and pre-empts false-progress moves
